section: §1.3 lane table (km 7.017–9.390, λ = 2), §1.4 cells 33–37, §2.1 group G3, §4.7 capacity grid, §6.1 F1 scope
proposed_change:
Before the commit:
1. Extend A1 to the lane count over km 7.518–9.217 (imagery or the IRIS r_node documentation).
2. Add a pre-registered pre-calibration fact (F16, calibration days): for every cell, the measured arriving flow per configured lane divided by B's real Q_dis per lane.
   - Arriving flow = median of the daily maximum 15-min flow, built from stations, measured ramps and balances.
   - Fixed rule: any non-B cell with a ratio > 1.10 blocks calibration until it is resolved, in this order:
     (a) a geometry correction from imagery (λ = 3 with an exit-lane end at X15 if confirmed, re-running the §1.4 cell rule);
     (b) otherwise, a separate capacity group G4 for cells 34–37 (v_f tied to G3; ρ_cr and a fitted), with its bounds, popsize and seeds stated now;

3. Disclose this inspection in §0.5. It used all 52 Wednesdays, validation days included.

Fix all three now, in this protocol:
(a) The re-centring rule for gate use. Either c_d is drawn from F̂ as estimated, or c_d / median(F̂) is used; pick one and state it. The c = 1 sensitivity stays reported.
(b) Gate the stochastic plant that the gate will actually use, with the 7,190,095 draws:
   - P3s: expected agreement ≥ 0.75, or Brier score ≤ that of the calibration-day daily-demand threshold classifier;
   - P6s: expected B-active share per demand half within k_h, and the gradient conditions (b)–(c);
   - both as gated rows next to P3/P6. A plant that passes only at c = 1 is 'deterministic-only' and cannot be used with F̂.
(c) If > 20 % of active calibration days are not reproducible, or the KM tail mass placed at 1.200 exceeds a stated share (e.g. 25 %), F̂ is declared not estimable. The stochastic element is then not usable for the gate (author decision, logged); this rule is written now.

Decide before the commit, not after validation:
(a) Make the merge variant the primary B geometry and report the weave reading as a sensitivity. Or:
(b) Keep the weave, but give cells 31–32 one pre-registered weave-capacity factor ω ∈ [0.6, 1.0] on ρ_cr, fitted with the base parameters (bounds and seeds stated now, disclosed as geometry-motivated [VERIFY a weave-capacity source]). c and F1 then act on cells 31–32 only, so the head can sit upstream of the OSR station.

In either case, add a §8.4 synthetic unit test, using bound-midpoint parameters: an overloaded B must give a corridor-rule episode at (Pioneer Tr, OSR) with OSR ≥ 20 mph faster, and none at (OSR, T.H.101).

Switch ramp o to the balance only if all of these hold:
(i) a Queue detector with 2023 data exists, and it corroborates the balance (|ΣQueue / ΣB − 1| ≤ 0.05 in both windows) while Passage does not;
(ii) |ΣPassage − ΣB| exceeds 3 % of the link's through flow (the §3.4 scale).

Otherwise keep Passage, leave the link in §3.4, and flag it. A ramp without a usable Queue detector (E3; E4's three-lane queue only if summed) never switches.

Disclose this inspection in §0.5.

Reword: 'A_B = boundary flow + every replayed entrance inflow up to and including E14 − every exit flow up to and including X13, measured or class-B (the replayed series used by the model)'.

Add a unit test: on a synthetic free-flow day, the travel-time-shifted A_B equals the model flow at the OSR station within 1 %.

- Set the variant targets and Δ on the calibration heavy days, using the F8 real CI, with everything else frozen.
- Specify now the domain of Δ for the variants (Δ < 0 allowed) and the η they use (the frozen F1 η, or 1.0 for the base plant).
- Add a unit test for Δ < 0 (no chattering, mass conserved).
- Alternatively, state R4 as an explicit, disclosed exception to §8.5.
Replace the sentence with the table derived from the rule and the resulting B-cell list, and include it in unit test 9.

problem:
'Free-flow steady state (ρ = q/(λ v_f), v = v_f)' is not a METANET steady state:
- V(ρ) < v_f for any ρ > 0, so the state relaxes;
- it uses the boundary flow in every cell and ignores ramps and splits.

Unit test 3 ('free-flow steady state is stationary') fails against this definition. The scores are unaffected because of the 1-h warm-up, but the specification and the test contradict each other.
proposed_change: Define the initial state as the free-flow-branch solution of λ_i ρ_i V(ρ_i) = q_i, with v_i = V(ρ_i) and q_i propagated from the 04:00 boundary flow through the 04:00 ramp inputs and split ratios. Unit test 3 uses that state.

problem:
L_r is the 2.5th percentile of the bootstrap real median r over the heavy **matched** days, which is a set the model chooses.
(i) **Loose at the expected n.** With a stylised normal r (median 0.984, SD 0.036 from the pooled IQR), my computation gives an expected L_r of about 0.950 at n = 6 and 0.955 at n = 8. On real data the review's evidence shows a CI of 0.931–0.991 for the n = 12 v0 validation half. So a plant with 3–4× the real median drop (r ≈ 0.95 or 0.93) passes. That is the failure of review issues 12 and 38, which Appendix A marks resolved.
(ii) **Perverse incentive.** The fewer heavy days the plant matches (down to 6), the wider the CI and the lower L_r, so a worse plant faces a laxer bound.
(iii) **Model-chosen reference.** Which days are matched decides the real reference, so the model can move it.
(iv) **Not paired.** It compares a model median with a CI of the real median, although the days are paired, against §8.5's single paired convention.
R4's low-drop GO requirement buffers the GO itself. But the primary plant is also the DRL training and evaluation plant (§1.1), where an exaggerated drop inflates any DRL-over-baseline gain. The rationale 'more drop ⇒ larger H' is stated as fact. It is a monotonicity inference (the review's issue 11 says 'my inference, not tested').
proposed_change:
Replace the P5b criterion with a paired one-sided rule at a fixed tolerance: median over the heavy matched days of (r_model,i − r_real,i) ≥ −0.02 [lab convention], with its CI reported.
- Freeze L_r once, before any model run, on a model-independent set: all n_H real heavy validation days, written into F11.
- Use that frozen L_r (a) as a second floor, median r_model ≥ L_r, and (b) for R4's high-drop variant.
- Keep the 'same days' CI version as reported only.
- Mark the H-monotone-in-drop argument in §0.4 and §5.3 as an inference, and name R4's low-drop requirement as the operative guard.

section: §4.7, §5.3 P6, §7 R3, §0.2 (the stochastic gate plant is never gated)
proposed_change:
Fix now in R3 whether c is re-centred (e.g. 'no re-centring' or 'c / median(F̂)'), and list F̂ in §0.2.

Add a gated P10 on the stochastic plant exactly as the gate will use it: 200 draws per usable validation day (seed 7,190,095), giving p_d = P(model B active).
- **(a) Over-confidence:** the number of days whose real B status had probability < 0.05 under the plant is ≤ the 95th percentile of its Poisson-binomial distribution under the plant.
- **(b) Skill:** the Brier score of p_d is ≤ the Brier score of a demand-half climatology fitted on calibration days.

Any stochastic P6 must use the Poisson-binomial distribution of the model counts, not the single-binomial k_h. A FAIL of P10 counts as a plant-gate FAIL (F1 re-derives F̂).

section: §5.1–§5.3 P2, P3, P4, P7(a), P5/P9 minima (model-dependent denominators)
problem:
Several statistics drop the plant's worst events from their own denominator.
- **P3** counts 'B active' at any time of day, so a model B episode in the AM on a day with a real PM episode counts as agreement.
- **P4** is computed over matched episodes only. Matching is within ±90 min, so the errors are capped by construction, and unmatched episodes are 'reported' only.
- **P7(a)** keeps only days where the matched model episode is ≥ 30 min, so days on which the model's episode is much too short are dropped, not scored.
- **P2**'s n_2 drops real-B days with no overlapping model episode.
At n_A ≈ 9 with P4's ≥ 6 matched, up to about a third of the real B events can be wrong-timed or missed and every row still passes. Separately, the model-side minimum (≥ 6 heavy matched days) equals the real minimum (n_H ≥ 6). At n_H = 6 a single miss FAILs P5, P7 and P9 together, while at n_H = 12 half can be missed. The stringency depends on the realised n, not on a stated rate.
proposed_change:
Anchor the denominators on real data, fixed before any model run:
- **P3:** a real-B-active day agrees only if a model B episode overlaps (±60 min) a real B episode; a real-inactive day agrees only if the model has no B episode.
- **P4:** over all real B episodes on usable validation days, with an unmatched episode scored as 90 min; PASS needs median ≤ 15 min **and** ≥ 75 % of real episodes matched [lab convention].
- **P7(a):** over all n_H real heavy days; the model duration is the matched episode's duration of any length, or 0 if unmatched.
- **P2:** denominator n_A; a day without an overlapping model episode counts as 'not at B'.
- **P5/P9:** require heavy matched days ≥ max(6, ⌈0.75·n_H⌉).

section: §3.2.1 vs §3.2.2, §3.5 E1, §5.1 (B active on usable days with an event-invalid B station; masking)
problem:
E1 requires fit-layer validity at both B stations: they are the β references for X12 and X13, and no entrance-free fallback exists. Fit-layer validity interpolates 30-s gaps of ≤ 15 min; event-layer validity needs ≥ 9 of 10 values per bin in ≥ 90 % of bins. So a usable day can have Pioneer Tr or Old Shakopee Rd event-invalid. The corridor rule then pairs consecutive valid stations, PT → T.H.101 (3.352 km) or Anderson Lakes / S of Highwood → OSR (3.28 / 4.31 km), all over the 3 km limit. No B pair exists, and 'B active' is False on both sides, because the model is masked by the same validity. That day counts as an automatic agreement in P3, adds to P6's inactive counts and lowers n_A. The corridor analysis already had 1 of 52 Wednesdays with a B station event-invalid (C1 valid_wed = 51).

The mask is also per station-day, not per bin. Real NaN bins (up to 10 %) break the 5-of-7 windows and the nanmean C4 windows, while the model has no NaN. So the 'identical' rule is not identical.
proposed_change:
Add to E1: 'both B stations (Pioneer Tr, Old Shakopee Rd) event-layer valid; otherwise the day is excluded (reason E1-B), counted per set before any model run'.

In §5.1, mask the model series **per bin**: model value = NaN wherever the real station's 5-min bin is NaN. Do this for every station used in P2–P9 and in the C4 windows.

(a) Run F1 only if the failure set includes a check its post-breakdown switch can affect: P1c, P4, P5a/P5b, P7 or P9. Otherwise the outcome is route stop.
(b) If F1's frozen Δ is bound-active at 0 (within 1 % of its range), record the outcome as 'base structure, second optimisation', not an F1 PASS, and send it to the author as a FAIL by default.
(c) Label every F1 PASS 'second look on the same validation days' in metanet_calibration.json and in every downstream result.

problem:
Several cleaning rules are circular, so several defensible implementation orders give different usable-day sets. Each is a forking path decided after data are seen.
- **Lane screen (§3.2.3)** pools over 'usable calibration days'. But usability (E1: ≥ 80 % of interior stations speed-valid) depends on speed-validity, which depends on the retained lanes from that same screen.
- **E4** compares each station with its median 'over the usable calibration days', a set E4 itself defines.
- **§3.4's 20 % rule** does not say which calibration days form the denominator: all 28, the days on which the link is closable, or the days passing E2/E3.
- **Q_A (§4.2)**, which feeds J's 0.5-weight term and P1c, does not say whether stations dropped by §3.2.4 (|c_s − 1| > 0.15) are excluded, although S_v does.

A_B = boundary + replayed entrances − 'every **measured** exit flow up to and including X13'. Read literally, the class-B exits are left out: the lumped T.H.62 sink X6+X7, W 78th St (X9) and I-494 EB (X10). According to the review (issue 28), the undetected exits carry about 40 % of the mainline flow at two interchanges. A_B would then exceed the model Q_dis for most of the day, excess would be huge and S2 = plateau/excess ≪ 1.2, so P9(2) FAILs mechanically. It is also unstated whether exits enter A_B as measured counts or as the replayed β·F. Either way the 'fix' would be chosen after seeing P9.
proposed_change: Define A_B = boundary flow + every entrance inflow as replayed (Passage, balance or Merge) up to and including E14 − every exit flow as replayed (class M counts and class-B balances, including X6+X7, X9 and X10) up to and including X13, each shifted by its free-flow travel time. Add a synthetic unit test in §8.4 checking that, in free flow, A_B equals the model's OSR + X13 flow within 1 %.

section: §5.3 P9(1) threshold vs the one-sided drop logic
problem: S1 = the maximum 15-min model flow in [onset − 60 min, end] / model Q_dis, required to be ≤ 1.05. That is an absolute upper bound on the pre-breakdown overshoot, i.e. a second drop-side constraint. §0.4 and §5.3 do not acknowledge it. It sits at the real data's own value: corridor v2's ratio of medians gives 1,938.0 / 1,850.4 ≈ 1.047, quoted in §5.5, and S1's window also includes post-onset bins. A plant reproducing the real overshoot is therefore near the threshold. Under the E14 balance replay its pre-onset OSR flow copies the real series (see the E14 issue), so P9(1) becomes close to a coin flip set by real detector noise. This contradicts the stated logic that a realistic drop must pass and only an exaggerated one may fail. R4's high-drop variant (Δ_drop = 1 − L_r ≈ 5 %) would also violate P9(1).
proposed_change:
Make P9(1) data-relative, in the same way as P5b:
- in the pre-calibration facts, compute the real S1 on calibration heavy days with the same window;
- gate paired on the validation heavy matched days: median(S1_model − S1_real) ≤ +0.03 [lab convention], or S1_model ≤ the frozen 97.5 % upper bound of the real S1.
State in §5.3 that P9(1) bounds the overshoot. Check the R4 variants against it.

section: §5.1 Q_dis, r 'C4 block applied unchanged' to the model
problem: The C4 block computes r on the day's **longest** episode at the pair. On the model side that may not be the episode matched to the real longest episode: for example, a longer spurious AM model episode at B, or two PM episodes. A heavy matched day is defined on the matched episode, but r_model and Q_dis,model would come from a different one. P7(a) uses 'the matched B episode', so the episode sets of P5 and P7 can diverge.
proposed_change: State that on the model side the C4 formulas are applied to the model episode matched to the real longest episode. P5a, P5b, P7 and P9 all use that same episode.

section: §8.5 vs §7 R4 and §5.5 (validation days used to set parameters)
problem: §8.5 says validation days 'filter the ensemble and nothing else'. But R4 measures Δ_drop on validation heavy matched days and sets the variants' Δ, by root-finding to ±0.5 pp, on those same days. Validation days thus fit gate-plant variants, so the statement is false. Also, the heavy matched set changes as Δ changes, so the root-finding target moves and ±0.5 pp may be unattainable; v1 gives no rule for that case.
proposed_change: Amend §8.5 to list R4's use: sensitivity variants only, never the primary plant. Fix R4's measurement set to the primary plant's frozen heavy matched days. Add a rule for when ±0.5 pp cannot be reached, e.g. 'use the nearest attainable Δ_drop and report it'.

problem: After an INCONCLUSIVE, the extension day set is open ('for example 2023 Tuesdays and Thursdays'). It is chosen after calibration and the §4.8 calibration-day diagnostics exist, so its composition (weekdays, months, how many) could be informed by model output. It is also unclear what 'both outcomes would be reported' refers to.
proposed_change: Fix the extension rule now. For example: all 2023 Tuesdays and Thursdays (with the request count stated), all treated as validation days under the same exclusions and minima, the list generated by code before any request, and no calibration-day result informing it. Define 'both outcomes' as the INCONCLUSIVE record plus the extended gate verdict.

section: §1.4 B cells, §1.6, §3.2.1 event layer 'unchanged', §4.7, §5.1–5.4 (P2, P4, P5, P7, P9), §6.1 F1, §7 R3/R4/R6; decision D3.2 premise
problem:
v1 treats Pioneer Tr → Old Shakopee Rd (B) as the corridor's active bottleneck. Cached 2023 data show an earlier, near-daily active bottleneck just upstream of B, which the v1 event layer cannot see. These are reviewer read-only estimates on the 52 cached Wednesdays, using the corridor rule.

(a) Frequency and timing. With Anderson Lakes speed taken from its one live lane (5423), the pair Anderson Lakes → Pioneer Tr qualifies on 27/51 Wednesdays, against 23/51 for B. On 15 of the 16 days with both, it starts first, a median 72 min before B's onset (range 40–140 min). On 11 days it occurs without B.

(b) Robust to the 5423 speed bias. 5423 reads about 10 mph below Pioneer Tr at free flow, but the full-valid S of Highwood Ave through lanes (7078/7079) show the same picture:
- in the hour before B's PM onset they run at a median 15–26 mph on 19/21 B days, while Pioneer Tr runs at 53–66 mph;
- they are below 40 mph for ≥ 60 consecutive minutes (13:00–20:00) on 45/51 Wednesdays, including 22 of the 28 days without B;
- median congested time is 130 min on non-B days and 190 min on B days.

(c) Mechanism. It is not exit-led at the Pioneer Tr exit: occupancy at 5427 stays at 0–3 % at every upstream onset (control 1.2 %). The likely head is the Anderson Lakes Pkwy entrance merge (E13, a controlled ramp, km 4.055) just after the 3→2 lane end at km 3.751. Discharge at the Pioneer Tr station during these episodes is 1,696 veh/h/lane (B: 1,850); r = 0.986 (IQR 0.947–1.024); median duration 55 min.

(d) Why the event layer misses it. The event layer drops Anderson Lakes on 43/52 days (lane 5424 dead). S of Highwood Ave → Pioneer Tr is then 3.145 km, above the 3 km pair limit, so the bottleneck is invisible on about 83 % of days to both the real and the masked model side.

Consequences:
- P2 is blind to it on most days. On the days Anderson Lakes is valid, P2 fails a correct plant, because the model's earliest overlapping episode would be at Anderson Lakes → Pioneer Tr.
- The capacity factor (§4.7), F1 and the R4 drop cells act only on cells 31–33, i.e. on the later, secondary bottleneck. H2's capacity classes (R3) inherit this.
- P9's free-flow-shifted arrivals at B overstate arrivals while the upstream queue holds vehicles, so S2 loses its meaning.
- §3.3.3/F12 attribute the queue at the I-494 merges to B.
- H2's VSL area '1.5–3 km upstream of B' would sit on the first bottleneck.
- C1 ('variable bottleneck') and D3.2's reason for adding Pioneer Tr rest on the same blind spot.
proposed_change:
Before the commit:

(1) Event layer. Amend the event layer, disclosed as an amendment to the corridor estimator. A station is event-valid for speed when its retained lanes are valid, as the fit layer already does, so Anderson Lakes enters via 5423 with its c_s-free raw-speed bias reported. Alternatively, admit the 3.145 km pair S of Highwood Ave → Pioneer Tr. Recompute the per-pair episode counts and first-breakdown location per day as a new pre-calibration fact (F10).

(2) Two bottlenecks. Define B1 = Anderson Lakes → Pioneer Tr (cells 26–30; E13 merge in cell 26) and B2 = Pioneer Tr → Old Shakopee Rd (cells 31–33).
- 'Real active' is defined per bottleneck.
- P2: the model's earliest episode is at the pair of the real earliest episode.
- P3/P4 for both.
- P5a discharge at the Pioneer Tr station for B1, as at Old Shakopee Rd for B2.
- P7 extent measured from the most upstream active head.
- P9 defined at the first-active bottleneck.

(3) Capacity factor and drop. Estimate the capacity factor per bottleneck (c1, c2, jointly on calibration days). F1 cells = B1 ∪ B2. Restate R3, R4 and H2's capacity classes on both.

(4) Mechanism diagnostic. Extend §1.6 to B1: X12 and the Anderson Lakes lane end.

(5) Author confirmation. Add a §0.6 item (A8): the author re-confirms D3.2 and the H1/H2 premise (which bottleneck the four controlled ramps and the VSL area target), now that the first breakdown is upstream and near-daily, before anything is calibrated.

section: §3.3.2 passage-vs-balance rule; §3.4 detector-fault rule; §7 R1(c)–(d) (mode C demand)
problem:
The 10 % rule compares the passage/balance ratio with the ramp's own volume. The balance, however, carries the mainline stations' error, and the mainline flow is about 15–30 times larger. Reviewer estimates on calibration days (fit-layer approximation, no ΔN term):

| Ramp | Passage (veh/day) | Queue (veh/day) | Balance (veh/day) | Passage/balance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Marth Rd (E12) | 1,280 | 1,402 | 2,548 | 0.50 |
| Anderson Lakes (E13) | 1,710 | 1,681 | 801 | 2.06 (mostly via the S of Highwood → Pioneer Tr fallback link) |
| Pioneer Tr (E14), for comparison | 7,090 | 4,498 | 4,618 | 1.54 |

The two residuals, +1,270 and −910 veh/day (+2.6 % and −1.8 % of mainline inflow), have opposite signs on the two links that share the S of Highwood Ave station. That is the signature of a roughly 2.5 % over-count at that station. The §3.4 rule (> 3 % on > 20 % of days) does not catch it: Highwood Ave → S of Highwood Ave has e median 2.6 % and exceeds 3 % on only 7 % of days. Because §3.3.2 fires first, both links become balance-closed and leave §3.4 entirely.

As written, both controlled ramps switch and are only flagged. Marth Rd is replayed at about 2× and Anderson Lakes at about 0.5× what both of their detectors count. Anderson Lakes is the merge at the first bottleneck (previous issue), so its δ_m term and the cell 23–25 flows are distorted.

In mode C, controlled ramps take Queue-detector demand (R1). The gate plant would therefore receive about 1,270 fewer veh/day at Marth Rd and about 900 more at Anderson Lakes than the validated replay. R1(c) P0 (5 %) would fail on almost every ramp-day at both, and the plant used by the gate would not be the one that passed §5.

Pioneer Tr is different: its Queue/balance ratio of 0.964 corroborates the switch.
proposed_change:
(1) Switch condition. Switch a ramp to the balance only if its Queue detector corroborates the balance (|ΣQueue/Σbalance − 1| ≤ 0.05 in both windows) and contradicts Passage. Otherwise keep Passage.

(2) Shared-station test, applied before the ramp rule. A station whose two adjacent closable links show opposite-sign residuals, each > 1 % of link inflow and within a factor of 2 of each other, on > 50 % of calibration days is marked flow-unreliable, and its links are merged (§3.4).

(3) Scale of the threshold. Also express the ramp threshold against link inflow: switch only if |balance − passage| > 0.10 × ramp volume AND > 1 % of link inflow.

(4) Controlled ramps. For E9, E12, E13 and E14, require now that the replay inflow and the mode-C demand come from detectors whose calibration-day daily totals agree within 5 %. Otherwise the ramp is listed, and the gate protocol must state the reconciliation before any gate run.

section: §4.2 S_q,d and the 'balance-closed → leaves the flow terms' rule; §5.3 P1a; §5.6 P-T
problem:
Applying v1's own rules to the cached data removes every flow station between km 0.37 and 9.39 from S_q,d:
- E12, E13 and E14 switch (previous issue);
- the class-B elements X9, X10 and E15 close I-494, Highwood Ave and T.H.101;
- E3 and E4 very likely switch as well (T.H.7 EB PM ratio 0.894; Excelsior Blvd 1.194 day / 1.122 PM), which also removes Excelsior Blvd and Lincoln Dr.

What remains is T.H.7, Van Buren Way, Bren Rd, 69th St, Valley View Rd and S of Valley View Rd (km −7.3 to +0.37), plus Anderson Lakes on about 9 days. These stations are free-flowing on essentially all days: S of Valley View Rd is below 45 mph during B on 0/23 B days. Their links close within a median 0.1–1.8 %.

Consequences:
- P1a (median NRMSE_q ≤ 0.10) is passed by conservation of the replayed inputs alone, so it cannot discriminate.
- J's 0.25 flow term carries no bottleneck information.
- The quoted 0.123 null was computed on a different station set.
- No flow or discharge quantity of the first bottleneck is checked anywhere.
- P-T (§5.6) gates the 2024 transfer on N0, P1a and P3 only, i.e. numerics, a check that cannot fail, and the B-active agreement.
- The plant is validated on Wednesdays only, while the gate draft draws 14-day sequences with every calendar type and tunes per-calendar-type comparators on 2023 days that are not pulled.
proposed_change:
(1) Congestion-window flow term. Keep the downstream stations of balance-closed links in a flow term restricted to the congestion windows: bins inside any real or model episode in Q_A ± 30 min, where the replay identity no longer holds. Alternatively, replay switched ramps as their Passage time profile scaled to the Queue-detector daily total, so the downstream station does not enter the input.

(2) Discharge at the first bottleneck. Gate the discharge at the first-active bottleneck (Pioneer Tr station), as P5a does at B.

(3) Re-anchor P1a. Recompute P1a's null reference on the actual S_q,d.

(4) Strengthen P-T. Add P1c and P4 (and P5a when n allows) to P-T.

(5) Calendar types. Add an R item: before the gate uses any calendar type other than Wednesday (in 2023 tuning or 2024 test), the frozen plant passes the strengthened P-T check on that day type. That needs an approved pull of those days.

section: §3.3.3 served merge flows, §0.2 scope, §7 R1(d) and R2
problem:
(a) Replay leak. The replayed I-494 merge counts (7108 + 7086) fall to a median 0.89 (IQR 0.84–0.94, n = 50 days) of their pre-queue level within 15–60 min after the S of Highwood Ave through lanes drop below 40 mph. This was not controlled for time of day (almost no PM-uncongested days exist), so it is an estimate. Roughly 175 of about 1,600 veh/h of input is withdrawn at the moment the real queue arrives. The plant therefore receives the real queue's timing through its input, and P3, P4 and P7 are partly scored on the outcome. R1(d) (mode C with meter rate = replay inflow) inherits the same leak, so it cannot detect it.

(b) R2 cannot be informative as written:
- The queue reaches the merges on almost every heavy day: Highwood Ave is below 45 mph in ≥ 30 % of B-episode bins on 20/23 B days, and the upstream queue lasts ≥ 60 min on 45/51 Wednesdays. 'Report separately with and without the queue at the merges' therefore has almost no 'without' days.
- An uplift fitted on uncongested days extrapolates from light to heavy days.
- The reconstruction is left to a later protocol, so it can be chosen after tuning-day behaviour has been seen.
- I knows the reconstructed demand exactly, so the uplift directly sizes H for about 50 % of the inflow to the first bottleneck. That makes it a forking path.
proposed_change:
(1) Reported 'no-leak replay'.
